# pipetail Blog

> By Engineers. For Engineers. Technical blog by pipetail covering Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS, Helm and cloud-native infrastructure.

Every post is also available as raw Markdown at its URL plus `index.md`. All posts in one file: https://blog.pipetail.io/llms-full.txt

## Posts

- [10 most common mistakes using terraform](https://blog.pipetail.io/posts/2020-10-29-most-common-mistakes-terraform/index.md): Common Terraform anti-patterns and how to fix them: remote state, secret management, version pinning, modules, documentation, and directory structure.
- [Improve visibility in Helm workflows with Werf!](https://blog.pipetail.io/posts/2020-10-20-werf/index.md): How Werf adds real-time deployment tailing and live pod status to Helm workflows, replacing blind waits with actionable feedback.
- [How would I proceed with Kubernetes deployments?](https://blog.pipetail.io/posts/2020-07-17-helm-free-deployment/index.md): Alternatives to Helm for Kubernetes deployments using Kustomize overlays for templating and Kapp for ordered apply with automatic garbage collection.
- [Helmfile basics: get your Helm flow organized](https://blog.pipetail.io/posts/2020-07-13-helmfile-basics/index.md): Getting started with Helmfile to orchestrate multiple Helm releases using label selectors, environment overrides, and SOPS-encrypted secrets.
- [10 most common mistakes using kubernetes](https://blog.pipetail.io/posts/2020-05-04-most-common-mistakes-k8s/index.md): Common Kubernetes mistakes: missing resource limits, misconfigured probes, no ingress controller, wrong autoscaling, weak RBAC, missing anti-affinity and PDBs.
- [More EKS tips to make your life easier](https://blog.pipetail.io/posts/2020-04-13-more-eks-tips/index.md): Practical EKS tips: IAM Roles for Service Accounts instead of kube2iam, Cluster Autoscaler scale-from-zero with ASG tags, and spot instance priority expander.
- [Getting started with PodSecurityPolicy on EKS](https://blog.pipetail.io/posts/2020-03-15-psp-on-eks/index.md): How to implement PodSecurityPolicy on Amazon EKS with proper RBAC bindings and why you must delete the default eks.privileged policy first.
- [GitLab Runner on EKS](https://blog.pipetail.io/posts/2020-03-05-gitlab-runner-on-eks/index.md): Step-by-step guide to running a self-hosted GitLab Runner on AWS EKS using Terraform and GitLab Kubernetes integration.
- [AWS Systems Manager Session Manager: bye bye bastion hosts!](https://blog.pipetail.io/posts/2020-02-24-amazon-ssm-session-manager/index.md): Replace bastion hosts with AWS SSM Session Manager for SSH access to private EC2 instances using IAM-based access control and session logging.
- [Applications are not easy, tracing is: context propagation](https://blog.pipetail.io/posts/2020-02-14-opentelemtry-context-propagation/index.md): How to propagate trace context across microservices with OpenTelemetry using W3C Traceparent headers in Go.
- [More complicated EKS scenarios: EKS managed worker nodes without internet access](https://blog.pipetail.io/posts/2020-02-12-eks-private-cluster/index.md): Setting up EKS managed nodes in a fully private VPC with no internet using VPC PrivateLink endpoints for ECR, EC2, and S3.
- [Applications are not easy, tracing is: a brief introduction to OpenTelemetry](https://blog.pipetail.io/posts/2020-02-09-opentelemetry-introduction/index.md): Introduction to distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry in Go, from basic stdout exporters to production-ready LightStep integration.
- [DAPR: introduction to Distributed Application Runtime](https://blog.pipetail.io/posts/2020-01-29-dapr-introduction/index.md): Building microservices with DAPR sidecars on Kubernetes: pub/sub messaging with NATS, state management, and service invocation in Go and Vue.
